security_audit.summary: All 152 static findings were adjudicated as false positives. URLs are inert QR or documentation examples, reconnaissance matches are poster-design prose, and Markdown fences were misread as shell backticks. The review script uses quoted filenames with fixed local PDF utilities and does not evaluate captured output; no prompt injection or semantic security issue was found.

content.value_statement: Dense research content is difficult to fit into a readable conference poster. This skill turns research material into structured, accessible LaTeX poster designs.
actual_capabilities: Compares beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter for different layout and customization needs.
Structures titles, methods, results, conclusions, references, and acknowledgments into two, three, or four columns.
Applies poster typography, color contrast, spacing, visual hierarchy, and accessibility guidance.
Integrates figures, equations, citations, institutional colors, and QR codes into poster plans.
Provides reusable LaTeX templates and a shell script for PDF dimensions, fonts, pages, file size, and image checks.
limitations: Requires an installed LaTeX distribution and relevant poster packages for compilation.
The included review script depends on pdfinfo, pdffonts, pdfimages, awk, and other local command-line tools.
Automated checks cannot judge scientific accuracy, visual balance, color appearance, or conference compliance.
Several helper scripts and the schematic generator named in the documentation are not included.

use_cases.title: Convert a paper into a poster
use_cases.description: Create a concise conference poster with a clear reading path, focused findings, and a practical figure plan.

use_cases.title: Standardize department posters
use_cases.description: Create a reusable poster structure with institutional colors, consistent typography, and print-ready dimensions.

use_cases.title: Refine a technical layout
use_cases.description: Compare LaTeX packages and improve an existing layout for accessibility, visual hierarchy, and large-format printing.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A0 portrait beamerposter from this abstract: [abstract]. Use three columns, accessible colors, and placeholders for three figures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a first conference poster from an abstract

prompt_templates.title: Plan a results-focused poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this paper summary into a three-column tikzposter plan: [summary]. Prioritize results, reserve half the area for visuals, and include contact details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Converting a completed paper into a visual presentation

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing source
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LaTeX poster source: [source]. Identify layout, typography, contrast, figure, and compilation problems, then propose precise revisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving a draft before conference submission

prompt_templates.title: Select and validate a package
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter for these requirements: [requirements]. Recommend one, define the layout, and provide a print-quality verification plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing an implementation for complex institutional requirements

output_examples.input: Create an A0 portrait poster from a methods-heavy abstract.
output: Recommended package: beamerposter for predictable institutional styling.
Layout: three columns with methods condensed into a workflow and results given the largest central area.
Quality plan: verify A0 dimensions, embedded fonts, image resolution, contrast, and one-page output.

output_examples.input: Review my poster PDF before printing.
output: Automated review covers page size, page count, file size, font embedding, and image inventory.
Manual review covers alignment, text size, visual balance, color, QR codes, references, and print scaling.

output_examples.input: Convert my paper into a poster outline.
output_examples.output: A concise sequence with motivation, focused methods, prominent findings, key conclusions, selected references, acknowledgments, and contact information.

best_practices: Provide the conference size, orientation, required sections, brand colors, and submission rules before drafting.
Use high-resolution figures and keep body text large enough for viewing from several feet away.
Compile early, inspect the PDF at full size, and test a reduced-scale print before submission.
anti_patterns: Do not paste a full paper into the poster or rely on long paragraphs.
Do not retain placeholder URLs, sample citations, logos, or institutional details.
Do not assume automated metadata checks replace visual review, proofreading, or conference specification checks.

faq.question: Which LaTeX packages does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter, with guidance for choosing among their layout models.

faq.question: Can it compile the poster?
faq.answer: It provides compilation commands, but your environment must contain LaTeX and the required packages.

faq.question: Does it create scientific figures?
faq.answer: It plans figure placement and integration. The schematic generator referenced by the documentation is not included in this skill.

faq.question: Can it review a generated PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. The included script checks dimensions, pages, file size, embedded fonts, and image inventory when required local tools are installed.

faq.question: Does it support custom poster sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers standard sizes and can adapt layouts when you provide exact dimensions, orientation, and conference requirements.

faq.question: Is the generated poster ready for printing?
faq.answer: Not automatically. You must inspect visual balance, proofread content, confirm colors, test QR codes, and verify printer specifications.
